source_refs.asserted_value: Combining an NSAID with an ACE inhibitor (e.g. lisinopril) or an angiotensin-receptor blocker (e.g. losartan) can blunt the blood-pressure-lowering effect and, more importantly, can reduce renal perfusion — the combination is sometimes described as part of a "triple whammy" when a diuretic is also present.

claims.text: Combining an NSAID with an ACE inhibitor like Lisinopril can reduce the effectiveness of Lisinopril in patients with kidney disease or those at risk for kidney damage.

source_refs.asserted_value: Caution is generally warranted, especially in older adults, patients with reduced kidney function, or those who are volume-depleted; renal function is often checked if the combination is used for more than a short course.
